typologies.label: Structuring
typologies.summary: Structuring — known colloquially as "smurfing" — is the deliberate breaking-up of cash deposits into amounts just under a currency-transaction reporting threshold (in the US, the $10,000 CTR line) to keep individual deposits below the reporting trigger while the account accumulates a large aggregate cash position. The structured cash is then moved onward — wired out to a single beneficiary — turning a pattern of small, evasive deposits into a laundering leg.
indicators: High share of cash deposits sitting just under the CTR reporting line
Deposit amounts clustered near (but under) the threshold rather than spread naturally
Round-number deposits inconsistent with the account's declared cash profile
Multiple deposits inside a rolling 7-day window
Deposit cadence inconsistent with normal payroll/business cash cycles
Deposits spread across several branches or ATMs on the same day or in the same window
Geographic spread inconsistent with the customer's declared home location
Structured-in cash wired out to a single downstream beneficiary
Wire timing shortly after the structured cash accumulates (short dwell)

typologies.label: Funnel Accounts
typologies.summary: A funnel account is a collection point: it receives many small, geographically-dispersed deposits from unrelated depositors, then rapidly moves the aggregated funds onward to a single downstream beneficiary before the pattern can be reviewed. It is the collection-side mirror of BA001 Structuring — where structuring conceals the deposit pattern beneath a reporting line, funnelling conceals the collection pattern behind volume and dispersion, then clears the account out fast.
indicators: Deposits sourced from many distinct regions inconsistent with a single local customer base
Depositor locations with no plausible relationship to the account holder's declared
A large number of distinct, apparently unrelated depositors feeding one account
Deposit sizes individually unremarkable, but the depositor count itself is anomalous
Funds clearing onward within hours of landing, with no plausible accumulation purpose
Passthrough timing inconsistent with the account's declared business cycle
Outbound funds concentrated on a single downstream beneficiary rather than dispersed
Beneficiary already flagged elsewhere in the network

typologies.label: Mule Accounts
typologies.summary: A mule account is a personal account used purely as a pass-through point: it receives illicit funds from one or more originators and forwards them onward almost immediately, retaining little or nothing for itself. It is the personal-account mirror of BA002 Funnel Accounts — where funnelling hides behind volume and dispersion on the collection side, muling hides behind an individual's identity and a thin personal-banking profile, moving money at a controller's instruction rather than the account holder's own initiative.
indicators: Outbound transfers landing within hours or days of the matching inbound funds
Balance held on the account never accumulating despite regular large inflows
Account opened in the weeks immediately before illicit flows begin
No prior transaction history consistent with genuine personal banking
Monthly throughput many multiples of the declared salary or stated income
Transaction profile inconsistent with the account holder's declared occupation
Shared device or IP address with other accounts already flagged as mules
Shared downstream beneficiary or forwarding destination across multiple accounts
A controller instructing multiple, apparently unrelated account holders

typologies.label: Circular Funds Flow
typologies.summary: A circular funds flow is a round-tripping loop: funds leave an originating account, pass through one or more intermediary accounts, and return to the same origin (or an account under the same control) having taken on the appearance of unrelated third-party activity along the way. It is BA003 Mule Accounts run backwards — where a mule forwards funds onward and never sees them again, a circular flow is engineered so the ORIGINATOR gets the funds back, laundered through the round trip itself.
indicators: Funds returning to the origin account within the same reporting cycle they left it
Balance movements that net to near-zero over the round trip despite large gross flows
Multiple intermediary accounts carrying the funds between origin and return
Intermediaries with no independent commercial rationale for holding the funds
Amounts moving hop to hop with negligible fee or FX erosion
Round-number consistency across legs inconsistent with genuine trade settlement
The full round trip completing in hours or a few days
Legs scheduled back-to-back rather than at a pace consistent with real commercial timing

typologies.label: Rapid Movement
typologies.summary: Rapid movement is the velocity / layering signal at the heart of correspondent-banking monitoring: funds land on an account and clear back out again almost immediately, resting only long enough to register a balance change before they are gone. It is not defined by who sent the money or where it ends up — those can look entirely ordinary on any single leg — it is defined by HOW FAST the funds move and HOW MUCH volume passes through an account relative to what it normally holds.
indicators: Inbound funds clearing back out within hours of arrival
Balance spikes that resolve to near-baseline within the same reporting cycle
Turnover many multiples of the account's own average balance
Throughput inconsistent with the account's declared purpose or segment
Outbound funds splitting across several distinct onward destinations
Destinations with no independent commercial rationale for receiving the funds
Outbound amounts tracking inbound amounts almost 1:1
Round-number consistency between inbound and outbound legs inconsistent with genuine

typologies.label: Dormant Reactivation
typologies.summary: Dormant reactivation is the behavioural-anomaly signal at the far end of the account lifecycle: an account that has sat idle -- sometimes for months, sometimes for years -- suddenly comes back to life with flows that dwarf anything it ever carried while active. The finding is not any single transaction on its own; a large deposit or a new counterparty can each look ordinary in isolation. What makes it a finding is the CONTRAST between the account's long silence and the size, shape and speed of what happens the moment it wakes up.
indicators: A reactivating inflow many multiples of the account's pre-dormancy average monthly
No gradual ramp-up -- the account jumps straight to elevated activity
Extended idle periods, often exceeding a year, before the reactivating inflow lands
No account-closure or re-KYC event during the dormant period
New counterparties appearing immediately after reactivation with no prior relationship
New geographies inconsistent with the account's established footprint
Outbound amounts tracking the reactivating inflow almost 1:1
Round-number consistency between the reactivating inflow and the outbound leg

typologies.label: Cash Intensive Activity
typologies.summary: A cash-intensive business is a legitimate cover for laundering physical cash: cash & carry wholesalers, currency exchange houses, laundromats, and similar operators that plausibly handle real cash every day. The tell is not the presence of cash — it is cash disproportionate to the business's own declared profile, layered with the tells that separate genuine trade volume from placement.
indicators: Cash share of turnover running multiples of the business's own peer-segment norm
Cash-to-turnover ratio inconsistent with the declared business type
Actual cash deposited materially exceeding the volume declared at KYC onboarding
No plausible business explanation for the growth in cash handled
Deposits landing with an unnaturally even size and cadence
Coefficient of variation far below what a genuine retail cash business exhibits
Deposited cash traceable to unrelated third parties, not the business's own sales
Linked entities or depositors with no plausible commercial relationship to the account

typologies.label: Layering
typologies.summary: Layering is the classic middle stage of money laundering: funds already placed into the financial system are pushed through a chain of transfers designed to sever the audit trail from their source before the proceeds are integrated into legitimate-looking assets. Unlike BA004 Circular Funds Flow (engineered to return to the originator), a layering chain has no obligation to close a loop — its only job is to put distance, opacity and jurisdictional friction between the seed account and wherever the funds end up.
indicators: Multiple transfer hops between the seed account and the funds' eventual destination
A trail that goes cold well before it reaches an identifiable beneficial owner
Intermediaries that are shell companies or nominee entities with no independent
Corporate registries that show recently-formed entities with no verifiable trading history
Cross-border routing through recognised secrecy or offshore jurisdictions
Jurisdiction choices inconsistent with the seed account's declared business geography
The seed amount split into multiple fragments across the chain
Fragments re-merged downstream in combinations that defeat simple amount-matching

typologies.label: Transaction Laundering
typologies.summary: Transaction laundering is a legitimate-looking merchant account used as a payment processing front for hidden third parties: a card-processing relationship underwritten against one declared business is quietly used to clear volume for merchants — or principals — the acquirer never screened. Unlike BA007 Cash Intensive Activity (physical cash disproportionate to a declared profile), the tell here runs through the CARD RAILS themselves.
indicators: Processed card volume running multiples of the merchant's own declared business volume
Volume growth with no plausible business explanation
Unrelated sub-merchants folded into the one boarded processing relationship
Multiple unconnected storefronts settling to the same underlying account
Transaction types inconsistent with the boarded merchant category code
A "retail goods" MCC clearing digital, subscription or cash-equivalent transaction types
An elevated refund/chargeback rate with no genuine customer dispute cycle
Self-refunds or test transactions inconsistent with real commerce

typologies.label: Peer Group Anomalies
typologies.summary: Most correspondent-banking analytics compare an account against a fixed, absolute threshold — a dollar cut-line, a transaction count, a ratio. Peer group anomaly detection compares an account against the STATISTICAL PROFILE OF ITS OWN PEER SEGMENT instead: accounts of a similar type, size and declared business purpose. A transaction volume that is unremarkable for a high-turnover corporate current account can be a strong deviation signal for a retail deposit account, and vice versa — a fixed threshold misses this, a peer-relative model does not.
indicators: Transaction volume running multiple standard deviations above the peer segment mean
Volume growth with no plausible peer-consistent business explanation
Turnover velocity (transactions per period) inconsistent with the peer segment's norm
A rate of fund movement that outpaces the segment's typical pattern
A product/channel footprint markedly narrower or wider than the peer segment's norm
Usage inconsistent with the account's declared segment and business purpose
An unusually wide or unusually concentrated counterparty footprint against the peer norm
A single anomalous counterparty accounting for a peer-inconsistent share of activity

typologies.label: Insider Trading
typologies.summary: Insider trading is dealing in a financial instrument while in possession of material non-public information (MNPI) — an earnings release, an M&A announcement, a regulatory decision — ahead of the event's public disclosure. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how large the trader's position build is relative to their normal activity, how close to the event the position was built, whether there is a documented information-access linkage between the trader and a source with early knowledge, and how much profit is realised once the event's price impact lands.
indicators: Position build materially larger than the trader's normal average position
Position sized and directed inconsistently with the trader's stated mandate
Position concentrated in a single issuer or a small basket around one event
Position build concentrated in the days immediately before the event
Order timing inconsistent with the trader's normal trading cadence
Documented contact events with a corporate insider, advisor or corporate-access
Contact frequency inconsistent with the trader's normal coverage relationships
Source has known access to the issuer's material non-public information
Realised profit disproportionate to the position's entry value once the event lands
Profit timing tightly coupled to the event's public disclosure

typologies.label: Market Manipulation
typologies.summary: Market manipulation is the artificial distortion of a security's price or volume to create a false or misleading impression of supply, demand, or price, so a position can be exited — or a benchmark can be gamed — at an advantage. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how large the price move is relative to the instrument's normal volatility, how concentrated the account's footprint is against total market volume, whether the trading is coordinated across linked accounts, and how much of the price move reverses once the manipulative window closes — the tell that the move was not inf
indicators: Price move materially larger than the instrument's normal volatility
Move concentrated in a short surveillance window rather than a sustained trend
Move inconsistent with any contemporaneous public news or disclosure
Account share of total market volume disproportionate to its normal trading pattern
Volume concentrated in a thin or illiquid instrument
Order flow inconsistent with the account's stated trading mandate
Multiple accounts trading in concert, in the same direction, in the same window
Linked accounts sharing common beneficial ownership, venue, or execution timing
Coordination frequency inconsistent with independent trading decisions
Price move largely unwinds once the manipulative window closes
Reversal timing tightly coupled to the account's own exit, not to any market news
Reversal magnitude disproportionate to the size of the original move

typologies.label: Spoofing
typologies.summary: Spoofing is placing orders on one side of an order book with no intention of letting them execute, in order to move the visible order book and induce other participants to trade at a manipulated price, then cancelling the spoof orders and executing genuine trades on the opposite side once the market has reacted. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how large a share of order value is never genuinely intended to execute, how fast those orders are cancelled before the market can treat them as real, how much visible depth on one side the spoof orders manufacture, and how much genuine
indicators: Order value materially larger than the trader's genuine execution history would predict
Orders sized and directed to move the visible book rather than to execute
Order flow concentrated in a single instrument or a small basket around one venue
Orders cancelled within seconds of placement, well inside normal market reaction time
Cancellation timing inconsistent with the trader's normal order-management cadence
Spoof orders manufacturing a majority share of visible depth on one side
Depth imbalance inconsistent with genuine two-sided liquidity provision
Imbalance timed to coincide with opposite-side execution
Genuine execution disproportionate to normal fill rates while the book is skewed
Execution timing tightly coupled to the spoof orders' cancellation

typologies.label: Layering
typologies.summary: This is ORDER-BOOK layering — staggering non-bona-fide orders across multiple price levels on one side of the book to create a false impression of depth or intent, moving the price or inducing other participants to trade against it, then cancelling the staggered orders before they are ever meant to execute. It is distinct from the AML "layering" typology, which moves illicit funds through successive transactions to obscure their origin; CM004 is a market-abuse pattern in the order book, not a money- laundering placement/layering/integration stage. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives
indicators: Orders staggered across a materially wide spread of distinct price levels
Order-book footprint inconsistent with the trader's stated mandate
Level distribution concentrated in a single instrument or venue
Orders placed far exceeding orders ever executed
Order flow inconsistent with the trader's normal order-to-trade profile
Order cadence timed to precede price movement rather than to trade
A material share of visible book depth created on one side by the staggered orders
Imbalance timed to coincide with other participants' order flow
Imbalance disproportionate to the trader's genuine position objective
Staggered orders pulled within seconds of the book moving
Reversal timing tightly coupled to a price move or a counterparty's response
Cancellation pattern inconsistent with genuine liquidity provision

typologies.label: Wash Trading
typologies.summary: Wash trading is trading that produces no genuine change in beneficial ownership — matched buy and sell orders crossed against each other, directly or through a small, concentrated ring of counterparties, to manufacture volume, mark a price, or create a misleading impression of liquidity or interest in an instrument. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how much of the account's own volume matches against its own opposing orders, whether the buy-side and sell-side beneficial ownership overlaps, how much reported volume exceeds the volume genuinely changing hands, and how concentrat
indicators: Self-matched volume materially larger than would occur from ordinary market making
Buy and sell orders entered in close time proximity at matching size and price
Self-matching pattern inconsistent with the account's stated trading strategy
Documented overlap between the buy-side and sell-side beneficial ownership
Common control, common directors, or common registered address across counterparties
Overlap inconsistent with an arm's-length trading relationship
Reported volume materially exceeding the volume reflecting genuine economic activity
Volume inflation concentrated around price-sensitive windows (close, index inclusion)
Reporting inconsistent with the instrument's normal turnover profile
Volume concentrated in one or two distinct counterparties
Counterparty concentration inconsistent with the account's normal execution spread
Counterparties clearing through a shared broker with no independent price discovery

typologies.label: Front Running
typologies.summary: Front running is a trader dealing on their own account ahead of a client order they know is coming, positioned in the same direction, then closing out once the client's order has moved the market. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how many seconds before the client's own order the trader's order was placed, how strongly the trader's pre-position direction correlates with the client order's direction, how disproportionate the profit captured is once the client order lands, and whether there is a documented knowledge linkage between the trader and the desk handling the client ord
indicators: Trader's own order placed only seconds before the client's order
Order timing inconsistent with the trader's normal execution cadence
Repeated pattern of dealing immediately ahead of the same client's flow
Trader's pre-position direction strongly correlated with the client order's direction
Position sized and directed inconsistently with the trader's stated mandate
Position concentrated around a single client's order rather than a market view
Realised profit disproportionate to the position's value once the client order lands
Profit timing tightly coupled to the client order's execution
Position closed out immediately after the client order completes
Documented contact events with the desk handling the client order in the 90 days
Contact frequency inconsistent with the trader's normal coverage relationships
Trader has access to the client order management system or desk communications

typologies.label: Pump and Dump
typologies.summary: Pump and dump is coordinated promotion of a thinly-traded, low-float instrument to inflate its price on false or misleading enthusiasm, followed by distribution of the promoter's (and colluding accounts') position into the retail buying the promotion creates. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how concentrated the account's pre-promotion accumulation of the free float is, how large the burst of coordinated promotional activity around the campaign is, how far the peak price runs beyond the instrument's baseline, and how much of the position is distributed into retail once the pri
indicators: Free-float share accumulated materially larger than a passive market position
Accumulation concentrated in a single thinly-traded instrument ahead of promotion
Position built quietly, ahead of any public promotional activity
Burst of coordinated posts, messages or accounts around a single campaign
Promotional content inconsistent with the instrument's public disclosures
Coordination frequency inconsistent with organic retail interest
Peak price materially above the instrument's pre-campaign baseline
Price spike timed tightly to the promotional burst
Price action inconsistent with any underlying corporate news
Volume distributed into retail disproportionate to the account's total position
Distribution timing tightly coupled to the peak of the promotional campaign
Retail buying concentrated in the window the price is inflated

typologies.label: Cross Market Abuse
typologies.summary: Cross market abuse exploits the link between an account's cash position and a correlated derivative — or a position that spans multiple trading venues — using a trade on one leg to move the price of the other. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how tightly the account's cash and derivative (or cross-venue) positions correlate, how many distinct venues or instruments the correlated activity spans, how much of the price impact on the primary instrument transfers to the correlated instrument, and how tightly synchronised the trades across venues are in time — the tighter the synchr
indicators: Correlation between cash and derivative (or cross-venue) positions materially
Correlated positions concentrated in a single issuer or a small instrument basket
Position direction consistent across venues, inconsistent with independent trading
Correlated activity spread across a growing number of distinct venues or instruments
New venues added to the pattern shortly before a price-sensitive move
Venue mix spanning cash, listed derivatives and OTC products
A material share of the price impact on the primary instrument showing up on the
Price-impact transfer disproportionate to the correlated instrument's normal
Trades across venues clustered within a tight time window
Order timing inconsistent with the account's normal cross-venue trading cadence

typologies.label: Benchmark Manipulation
typologies.summary: Benchmark manipulation is the deliberate skewing of a regulated fixing — a reference rate, an FX fix, a commodity settlement price — through order flow concentrated in the closing seconds of the fixing window, when there is no longer time for the market to absorb it. The finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how much of an account's total daily volume is concentrated inside the fixing window itself, how far the resulting price deviation runs beyond the instrument's normal deviation for that window, how close to the window's close the order was placed, and whether the same account shows
indicators: Volume concentrated inside the fixing window materially larger than the account's
Order sizing inconsistent with the account's stated trading mandate
Concentration clustered around a single benchmark or a small basket of fixings
Fixing price deviation running far beyond the instrument's normal deviation for that
Price impact reverting sharply once the fixing window closes
Distortion inconsistent with contemporaneous market-wide moves
Orders placed in the final seconds before the fixing window's close
Order timing inconsistent with the account's normal execution cadence
Timing precision that leaves no window for the market to absorb the flow
Multiple prior fixing windows showing the same concentration-and-timing signature
Repeat pattern concentrated on the same benchmark or the same issuer
Escalating repeat frequency without a corresponding change in mandate

typologies.label: Suspicious Order Patterns
typologies.summary: Suspicious order patterns are the family's purely order-flow-behavioural typology: quote stuffing, momentum ignition, and abnormal cancel/amend rates. There is no single rule that condemns a trading account here — the finding is a convergence finding: it lives in how abnormal the cancel/amend rate is, how intense the peak order-submission rate is, how far price moves after an order burst relative to the instrument's normal move, and how far the average order size departs from the account's normal size.
indicators: Cancel/amend rate far beyond what genuine trading activity produces
Cancellations clustered in short bursts rather than spread across the session
Orders entered and withdrawn before any realistic chance of execution
Peak order-submission rate well beyond the account's normal cadence
Submission bursts timed around key price levels or reference points
Order-book depth distorted by high-frequency, low-intent order flow
Price move after the order burst well beyond the instrument's normal move
Directional move immediately following a cancel/amend or submission spike
Move not corroborated by underlying news, fundamentals or genuine volume
Average order size well beyond the account's normal size
Size anomaly concentrated in the same window as the order burst
Order sizing inconsistent with the account's declared trading mandate

typologies.label: Cryptocurrency Evasion
typologies.summary: Cryptocurrency Evasion is the use of virtual assets — wallet clusters and virtual-asset service providers (VASPs) — to move value around sanctions. It sits under the Crypto & Market Intelligence line (hence the CMI prefix) but ships in the sanctions suite because the exposure it measures is a sanctions exposure.
indicators: Direct exposure to a sanctioned wallet
Mixer / tumbler use
Unregistered VASP
VASP registered in a sanctioned jurisdiction
VASP in a high-risk jurisdiction
Counterparty sanctions exposure or adverse media
Owner designated, or in a sanctioned / high-risk jurisdiction

typologies.label: Entity Resolution
typologies.summary: FND001 Entity Resolution is the foundation capability that resolves duplicate representations of one real-world entity into a single canonical identity, so that risk attaching to any representation attaches to all of them.
indicators: Unresolved duplicate understating exposure across every downstream product
Name gate cleared but the match carried thereafter by address alone
Name gate cleared but the match carried thereafter by telephone alone
Names align while registration numbers differ
Address shared by many otherwise dissimilar names
Merge uniting entities incorporated in different registries
Match score near a confidence band boundary
typologies.intelligence_question: Which of these records describe the same party, and how confident are we?

typologies.label: Relationship Discovery
typologies.summary: FND002 Relationship Discovery is the foundation capability that derives typed, confidence-scored edges between resolved entities from six independent evidence sources, and reduces them to one non-duplicated set.
indicators: Shared attribute edge read as evidence of control
Dense shared attribute cluster, the signature of a formation agent
Control edge sitting at exactly its default confidence
Ownership edge sitting at exactly its default confidence
Control asserted with no transactional edge between the parties
Transaction edge recorded from one side only
Edge whose only evidence source is an address match
typologies.intelligence_question: What connects these two entities, on what evidence, and how firmly?

typologies.label: Beneficial Ownership Intelligence
typologies.summary: FND003 Beneficial Ownership Intelligence is the foundation capability that traverses ownership and control edges backwards from a subject entity to the parties standing at the top of its chains, computing each one's effective stake and the confidence of the path that establishes it.
indicators: Deep chain whose multiplied stake falls below the twenty-five percent threshold
Chain reaching exactly six hops, where traversal stopped rather than finished
High path confidence averaged over one weak edge
Circular ownership, leaving the structure with no terminal
Ownership edge carrying no stated percentage
Effective ownership computed over a chain with missing percentages
Single owner sharing many target entities
typologies.intelligence_question: Who ultimately owns or controls this entity, through what chain, and how much of that chain is actually evidenced?

typologies.label: Network Risk Assessment
typologies.summary: FND004 Network Risk Assessment is the foundation capability that combines five weighted risk components into a single network risk score, a band, a set of named drivers, and a confidence figure derived from the evidence underneath.
indicators: Component reading exactly zero, which may mean unsupplied rather than absent
Sanctions exposure edge diluted by volume into the relationship mean
Ownership edge typed OWNS, PARTIAL_OWNER_OF, SHAREHOLDER_OF or ULTIMATE_OWNER_OF
Confidence reported as one over evidence that carried no confidence at all
High structural score on a large but otherwise ordinary network
Ownership depth at three or above, where the component is already capped
Score sitting just below a band boundary
typologies.intelligence_question: How risky is this entity network, and which part of it carries the risk?

typologies.label: Investigation Workflow Intelligence
typologies.summary: FND005 Investigation Workflow Intelligence is the foundation capability that converts scored intelligence products into a ranked work queue, combining risk, confidence, exposure, materiality and complexity into a priority score, a band, named drivers and a queue assignment.
indicators: Priority read as risk, where the bands share names with FND004 and mean otherwise
Exposure silently defaulted to the risk score, putting most of the weight on one number
Materiality defaulted to fifty, where the product is unmeasured rather than neutral
Confidence reported between zero and one on a zero to a hundred scale
Well evidenced moderate finding outranking a weakly evidenced severe one
High complexity raising priority, counting the cost of work as a reason to do it sooner
Critical priority carrying no risk driver in its list
typologies.intelligence_question: Of everything the platform has produced, what should an investigator open first, and why that?

AIS transmission gaps on the true leg
Ship-to-ship transfers near the hub
True origin in a sanctioned jurisdiction
Hub in a high-risk free zone
Counterparties carrying sanctions exposure or adverse media

typologies.label: Front Companies
typologies.summary: A front company is an entity with little or no genuine economic substance, established to give a sanctioned interest a clean commercial face. It exists to transact — to hold accounts, sign contracts and move goods — while the real party stays hidden behind it.
indicators: No employees
No physical premises
No web presence
Generic business description
Recently incorporated
Dormant
Ownership linked to a designated party
Opaque ownership
Offshore owner
Secrecy / low-transparency incorporation (e.g. Marshall Islands)
Counterparties carrying sanctions exposure or adverse media

typologies.label: Name Screening Evasion
typologies.summary: Name Screening Evasion is the defeat of list-based screening through the *form of the name*: aliases, transliterations, suffix variants, deliberate misspellings and word re-orderings that let a listed party transact under a name an exact-match filter never flags. The party is on the list; the name on the paperwork is engineered not to match it.
indicators: A STRONG / FUZZY (non-exact) match above the 0.85 threshold — a variant that still resolves to a listed party
A match landing on an alias rather than the primary listed name
Multiple near-duplicate entities matching the same listed party
Sanctions-list hit (severity 90)
PEP hit (severity 70)
Adverse-media hit (severity 55)

typologies.label: Trade Based Sanctions Evasion
typologies.summary: Trade-Based Sanctions Evasion moves value or prohibited goods across a sanctioned boundary by manipulating the trade transaction itself — mispricing an invoice, or misdescribing the goods so that a controlled item travels under an innocuous label. The transaction is the instrument of evasion.
indicators: Large price deviation from benchmark (over/under-pricing)
Goods misdescription (declared ≠ actual)
High-value cargo under generic descriptions
Sanctioned destination
Counterparty sanctions exposure or adverse media
Trading party owned by / linked to a designated party

typologies.label: Dual Use Goods
typologies.summary: Dual-use goods are items with a legitimate civilian use that can also serve a military or proliferation purpose — electronics, precision instruments, controlled technology. Sanctions and export controls turn on the commodity's classification, its end-use and its destination, not merely on the parties named.
indicators: Dual-use / export-controlled classification
Military end-use
Controlled technology transfer
Sanctioned / embargoed destination
High-risk destination
End-user sanctions exposure or adverse media
End-user owned by a designated party
Opaque end-user ownership

typologies.label: High Risk Jurisdictions
typologies.summary: High-Risk-Jurisdiction exposure measures how much of an entity's footprint — where it is registered and operates, the corridors it trades, who owns it, who it deals with — touches sanctioned, embargoed or high-risk jurisdictions. Here the jurisdiction is not an aggravating detail behind another finding; it *is* the finding.
indicators: Two or more sanctioned jurisdictions in the footprint
One sanctioned jurisdiction alongside a high-risk jurisdiction
Three or more high-risk jurisdictions
Trade with a sanctioned jurisdiction
High-risk trade corridor
Owner designated, or registered in a sanctioned / high-risk jurisdiction
Counterparty sanctions exposure or adverse media

typologies.label: Complex Ownership Structures
typologies.summary: Complex Ownership Structures use structural opacity itself as the evasion mechanism: deep layering, circular holdings, nominee tiers and clusters of secrecy-jurisdiction incorporations engineered so that no reader can trace ultimate control. The structure need not resolve to a *named* designated party to be a finding — the opacity is the risk.
indicators: Layering depth ≥ 4–5
Circular ownership loop
Two or more nominee tiers
Shared directors across nodes
Shared registered addresses
Multiple shell indicators
Multiple secrecy jurisdictions (BVI, Cayman, Panama, Seychelles)
Counterparties carrying sanctions exposure or adverse media

typologies.label: Over Invoicing
typologies.summary: Over-invoicing is a common Trade-Based Money Laundering technique whereby the price of goods is intentionally inflated beyond their true market value.
typologies.intelligence_question: Are import or export transactions being deliberately over-invoiced to facilitate the movement of illicit value across borders?

typologies.label: Over Invoicing (Cross-Domain)
typologies.summary: Over-invoicing is a common Trade-Based Money Laundering technique whereby the price of goods is intentionally inflated beyond their true market value.
typologies.intelligence_question: Are import or export transactions being deliberately over-invoiced to facilitate the movement of illicit value across borders?

typologies.label: Under Invoicing
typologies.summary: Under Invoicing occurs when the value of goods or services on an invoice is intentionally understated below their true market value. It is the mirror of over-invoicing: where over-invoicing moves value to the *exporter* through overpayment, under-invoicing moves value to the *importer* — the buyer receives goods worth far more than the price paid, and the difference is settled or realised outside the visible trade.
indicators: Invoice Deflation
High Value Trade
High Risk Corridor
Related Party Trading
Shell Company Structure
Repeat Activity
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a trade transaction being used to transfer value through invoice deflation below expected market value — understating the price to move value to the importer, evade duty, or settle an obligation outside the visible trade?

typologies.label: Multiple Invoicing
typologies.summary: Multiple Invoicing raises more than one invoice against a single underlying shipment of goods, so that one legitimate movement of goods justifies several payments. Each invoice looks ordinary in isolation; the abuse is only visible when they are reconciled against the one shipment they all reference.
indicators: Duplicate Invoicing
Repeated Settlement
High Value Trade
High Risk Corridor
Related Party Trading
Shell Company Structure
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a single shipment being invoiced multiple times to justify several payments for one movement of goods, transferring value under the appearance of legitimate trade?

typologies.label: Phantom Shipping
typologies.summary: Phantom Shipping settles or invoices a trade for goods that were never actually shipped. There is a payment, an invoice and often a contract, but no genuine movement of goods — the shipping record is missing, forged, or inconsistent with the trade. The trade exists only on paper to justify a cross-border payment.
indicators: Missing Shipment
No Bill of Lading
Document Discrepancy
Payment Without Delivery
Related Party Trading
Shell Company Structure
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a trade being settled or invoiced for goods that were never actually shipped — a payment with no genuine movement of goods behind it?

typologies.label: False Description Of Goods
typologies.summary: False Description of Goods declares a consignment as something other than what actually ships — a different commodity, HS code, quality or control status. The misdescription lets the trader misstate value, conceal a controlled or high-value item, evade duty, or move value under cover of an innocuous commodity.
indicators: Commodity Mismatch
HS Chapter Mismatch
Controlled-Goods Concealment
High Value Trade
Related Party Trading
Shell Company Structure
typologies.intelligence_question: Do the goods as declared match the goods that actually ship — or is a false description being used to conceal the true commodity, its value, or its control status?

typologies.label: Circular Trade
typologies.summary: Circular Trade (round-tripping) cycles goods or funds through a chain of related parties so that value leaves an entity and returns to it with no genuine change of ownership or economic purpose. Each individual trade looks legitimate; only when the chain is assembled does the loop appear — the same goods, or the value they represent, come back to where they started.
indicators: Closed Trade Loop
Common Control
Round-Tripped Value
High Value Trade
Shell Company Structure
High Risk Corridor
typologies.intelligence_question: Do goods or funds cycle back to their origin through a chain of related trades — a closed loop with no genuine change of ownership?

typologies.label: Dual Use Goods
typologies.summary: Dual Use Goods are items with a legitimate civilian use that can also serve a military or proliferation purpose — electronics, precision instruments, controlled technology. When such goods move through trade, the risk turns on the commodity's classification, its end-use and its destination, not merely on the parties named. Trade in dual-use goods can be used to divert controlled items to prohibited end-uses under cover of ordinary commerce.
indicators: Dual-Use Commodity
Military End-Use
Controlled Technology
High Value Trade
Related Party Trading
Shell Company Structure
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a trade moving a dual-use or export-controlled commodity — and does its end-use, technology content and destination indicate diversion to a prohibited purpose?

typologies.label: Third Party Payment Abuse
typologies.summary: Third Party Payment Abuse settles a trade through a payer who is not the trade counterparty — an unrelated third party, split settlement, or a payment that does not match the trade. The payment breaks the link between the trade and the funds, letting value enter or leave under cover of a legitimate-looking transaction while the true source or destination of the money is obscured.
indicators: Third-Party Payer
Split Settlement
Payment Mismatch
High Value Trade
Related Party Trading
Shell Company Structure
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a trade being settled by a payer who is not the trade counterparty — an unrelated third party, split, or mismatched payment that breaks the link between the trade and the funds?

typologies.label: Shell Company Trading
typologies.summary: Shell Company Trading routes trade through a counterparty with no genuine commercial substance — no employees, premises, trading history or economic footprint — used to give illicit trade a legitimate commercial face. The shell exists to transact: to hold accounts, sign contracts and settle payments while the real party stays hidden behind it.
indicators: Shell Counterparty
No Commercial Footprint
Related Party Trading
High Value Trade
High Risk Corridor
Recently Incorporated
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a trade being routed through a counterparty with no genuine commercial substance — a shell used to give illicit trade a legitimate face?

typologies.label: Sanctions Evasion Through Trade
typologies.summary: Sanctions Evasion Through Trade uses ordinary-looking trade to move value or goods to or from a sanctioned party or jurisdiction. The trade documents describe a legitimate transaction, but a party to it — or the jurisdiction it touches — is subject to sanctions. Trade becomes the vehicle for maintaining a commercial relationship that direct payment or name screening would block. This is the most severe of the TBML typologies.
indicators: Sanctioned Party
Sanctioned Jurisdiction
High Risk Jurisdiction
High Risk Corridor
Shell Company Structure
Related Party Trading
typologies.intelligence_question: Is a trade being used to move value or goods to or from a sanctioned party or jurisdiction — maintaining a commercial relationship that sanctions prohibit?

typologies.label: Freight Cost Inflation
typologies.summary: Freight Cost Inflation occurs when value is displaced out of the goods line and into the ancillary charges on a trade document — freight and insurance — where nobody benchmarks it.
indicators: Freight Above Benchmark
Insurance Cost Inflation
Incoterm Freight Mismatch
Cap Hugging
Cap Circumvention Composite
Unbenchmarked Route
typologies.intelligence_question: Is value being displaced out of a benchmarked or capped goods line into freight and insurance charges that are not benchmarked — so that the trade appears correctly priced while the real transfer happens in the ancillary costs?
